chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
He was asked about a man who sold an item which was not with him, for a specified term, and guaranteed the sale to him. He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it / it is permissible
key_terms.لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ: not with him / not in possession

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell something you do not currently possess in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the concept of *bay' al-ma'mur* (selling what is not yet in possession) by emphasizing the seller's guarantee (*daman*) for delivery within a specified term, a key distinction in Shia fiqh from the stricter Hanafi view. It reflects the practical flexibility of Ja'fari jurisprudence in facilitating trade and credit transactions, provided the risk of non-delivery is borne by the seller. This ruling underscores the principle that ownership and possession can be decoupled in commercial contracts when accompanied by a binding guarantee.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Mansour, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who sold an item which was not with him, to a (specified) term, and guaranteed the sale to him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mansur from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
was asked about the case of a man who makes a sale for an appointed time without having the merchandise with him and guarantees the sale for the buyer. He (the Imam) said, Tt is not unlawful.’”.
